concepts.why: The presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components in the left maxillary sinus, erosion of the orbital floor and maxillary walls, and displacement of the inferior rectus muscle without invasion, are consistent with a diagnosis of Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma.

The presence of a spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells, rare mitotic activity, and no cytologic atypia, are consistent with a diagnosis of Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma.

The presence of a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus, erosion of the orbital floor and maxillary walls, and displacement of the inferior rectus muscle without invasion, are consistent with a diagnosis of Esthesioneuroblastoma.
The presence of sinus pressure, facial swelling, and external deviation of the nasal septum, are consistent with a diagnosis of Invasive Fungal Sinusitis.
The presence of sinus pressure, facial swelling, and a left nasal mass, are consistent with a diagnosis of Nasal Polyps.
The presence of mild left-sided proptosis and erosion of the orbital floor, are consistent with a diagnosis of Orbital Trauma.
The presence of external deviation of the nasal septum and a left nasal mass, are consistent with a diagnosis of Nasal Fracture.
The presence of sinus pressure, facial swelling, and a left nasal mass, are consistent with a diagnosis of Sinusitis.
